- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes — add a small lagged correction (e.g., -0.5 to -1.0 of the spike’s magnitude).
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Mean-reversion bias in long-term forecasts (15+ days) — if sentiment is flat or bearish, reduce forecast slope toward recent mean.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price fails to rise — model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation from recent mean.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment shifts sharply, delay forecast adjustment until 3–5 days later.
